To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the habitual music-listening is not associated with physiological or psychological functioning.

qualitative, but not quantitative, aspects of habitual music listening are related to physiological and psychosocial functioning and that this relation is mediated by emotion regulation and stress-reactivity.
qualitative aspects of habitual music listening, such as the reasons for listening, are related to physiological and psychosocial functioning.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether habitual music-listening behavior is associated with physiological and/or psychological functioning.
the question of whether and how habitual music-listening behaviours influence physiological and psychological functioning, which is of particular interest in the context of the COVID-19 pandemic.
the relationship between habitual music-listening and physiological and psychological health.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the habitual music-listening behaviours are not directly associated with physiological and psychosocial functioning, but are mediated by the individual stress reactivity and distress-augmentating emotion regulation.
the beneficial effects of music listening depend on the specific music-listening context, and the reasons for listening.

music-listening behaviour does not seem to be a general factor that has a positive effect on physiological and psychological functioning, but rather a multifaceted and complex behaviour that is influenced by a variety of factors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the habitual music-listening behavior is not a homogeneous behavior, but is influenced by dispositions and is not obviously linked with physiological or psychological functioning.
listening to music is not a panacea for all kinds of problems.
listening to music has no direct effects on health, but may influence health indirectly via the regulation of emotions and stress.
The main takeaway from our work is that

it is important to consider the context of music listening, as well as the individual dispositions of the listener, in order to fully understand the effects of music listening on physiological and psychological functioning.
music listening may not have the same effects in all individuals, which may be related to the reasons for music listening.
the reasons for listening to music, and not the amount or the relevance of music, are related to psychological and physiological outcomes.
